title: Physics of the flying fish: glide data and Thompson's flight envelope
headline: TFF v2 (HYPOTHETICAL co-design map, no bird data): with Lean's C14 binding, a truly-flying 60 g fish is a region, not a point: feasible pairs of wing loading and aerobic O2 capacity shrink with altitude on both axes, but within the troposphere to 5 km the boundary moves by about 30 percent while the real fish sits 30x below it, so the gap is O2 delivery, not wings. The TFF point (12 N/m2, 1.31 W aerobic) reaches a 1000 m target (bat reference) only with a cardiac output 36x the sourced fish maximum or an air-breathing surface taking up 450 ml O2/min/kg in air, which no fetched source sizes; its map ceiling is 2.7 km; in the sim it climbs at 0.15 m/s. Winged zebrafish (0.51 g, v_min 6.1 m/s = 205 body lengths/s): could glide if launched, cannot launch itself. Co-evolution of wings and O2 processing: no comparative evidence found either way (logged search); stays a hypothesis. Launch drag threshold on chain power: body Cd <= 0.01 and lobe Cd <= 0.1. Earlier results unchanged: real fish inside Thompson's envelope; sustained aerobic flight eliminated by Lean C14; 13 unsigned nanopub drafts; birds excluded throughout.
